transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The 4C error code on your Samsung dishwasher (DW60M6050FS) specifically indicates a water inlet issue. This means the machine is not detecting water entering the tub within the expected time frame. The beeping confirms an active fault that prevents the cycle from starting.

Here are the steps to troubleshoot and resolve this, ordered from most common/easiest to more complex:

### 1. Check Your Home Water Supply
• Is the water valve open? Ensure the hot water tap under your sink (or behind the dishwasher) is fully turned on.
• Check for kinks: Inspect the water supply hose behind the dishwasher for any bends or kinks that might restrict flow.
• Low water pressure: If other appliances in your home are also having low water pressure, this could be a building-wide issue.

### 2. Reset the Dishwasher
Sometimes the control board needs a reset to clear the error:
1.  Turn off the dishwasher using the power button.
2.  Unplug it from the wall socket or turn off the circuit breaker for 5–10 minutes.
3.  Plug it back in and try starting a cycle again.

### 3. Inspect the Water Inlet Valve Filter (Most Common Fix)
Over time, sediment or debris can clog the filter screen inside the water inlet valve, preventing water from entering.
• Turn off the water supply to the dishwasher.
• Disconnect the water supply hose from the back of the dishwasher.
• Look into the port on the dishwasher where the hose connects. You should see a small mesh filter.
• Remove it carefully (if accessible) and clean it with a soft brush under running water. If you can’t reach it, you may need to remove the inlet valve assembly from the bottom of the unit for better access.
• Reconnect the hose and turn the water back on. Check for leaks before powering up.

### 4. Check the Water Inlet Valve
If cleaning the filter doesn’t work, the water inlet valve itself may be faulty or stuck closed.
• This is an electronic component that opens to let water in when the cycle starts. If it fails electrically or mechanically, no water will enter.
• You can test this with a multimeter for continuity if you’re handy, but replacement is often simpler. The part number for your model is typically DA62-17058A (verify with your specific serial number).

### 5. Check the Water Pressure Switch / Level Sensor
Less commonly, the water level sensor may be faulty or clogged with debris, sending a false signal that no water has entered. This usually requires professional diagnosis.

---

### What to Do Next:
1. Try steps 1 and 2 first (check water supply and reset).
2. If the error persists, clean the inlet filter (Step 3). This resolves the majority of 4C errors.
3. If cleaning the filter doesn’t help, you likely need to replace the water inlet valve.

If you’re uncomfortable performing these steps, contact Samsung Support or a qualified appliance repair technician. Since your model is relatively recent (DW60M series), it may still be under warranty if purchased within the last 1–2 years.

Checked the valve under the sink, it's a screwdriver-slot one and the slot was at 90 degrees, so it was turned off. I turned it on and the dishwasher now fills and runs normally. No kinks in the hose and the pressure at the kitchen tap is fine. I'd also done the power reset, which made no difference until the valve was open.

It’s great that you’ve identified the root cause! The 4C error code on Samsung dishwashers specifically indicates a water inlet issue, and in your case, it was simply due to the water supply being turned off at the valve under the sink. With the valve now open, the dishwasher is functioning normally again.

To summarize what likely happened:
• The 4C error occurs when the dishwasher doesn’t detect water entering within a set time frame.
• Since the water supply was closed, no water could enter, triggering the error and preventing any cycles from starting.
• Once you opened the valve, the dishwasher received water as expected, allowing it to resume normal operation.

### Tips for Future Prevention:
1. Regular Checks: If you notice similar issues in the future, always double-check that the water supply valve is fully open before troubleshooting further.
2. Filter Maintenance: Periodically clean the inlet filter inside the dishwasher (as mentioned earlier) to prevent clogs from sediment or debris.
3. Power Resets: While a power reset can help clear minor glitches, it won’t resolve issues caused by external factors like water supply problems.

If this issue recurs despite the valve being open, you may want to inspect the inlet hose for kinks or check the inlet valve itself for potential faults. However, based on your experience, it seems everything is working as intended now!
